name: Grandport
basis: Grandport in Neokosmos, a dark fantasy world by Oak (https://quietoak.github.io/NeokosmosWiki/, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), included with Oak's permission.
summary: The merchant republic's capital, built on oak piles in a shifting estuary: steep timber gables, stone counting houses and merchant palaces on stone rafts. Ten years after the Revolution, the Merchant Circle rules and royalists still whisper about the exiled prince.

wiki.title: Neokosmos Wiki: Children of Sol Eternel, The Steel and the Sun

inferred.note: Everyday places, careers, holidays and their dates, food, prices, climate and the exact district layout are invented in the setting's voice to give the city street-level detail. Correct freely. Coordinates are a stand-in grid for distances only.

neighborhoods.name: The Raft Palaces
neighborhoods.summary: Merchant princes' palaces of carved ashlar floating on six-foot stone rafts laid in the drained marsh, with Lord Edgar Grandeholm's great tower above them all. Household guards and quiet gardens.

neighborhoods.name: The Ledger Quarter
neighborhoods.summary: Old timber houses underpinned with stone counting houses on the ground floor: insurers, brokers, notaries and the chambers where the Merchant Circle and the commons' house sit.

neighborhoods.name: Guild Gables
neighborhoods.summary: The steepest, most competitive front-facing gables in the city: timber-framed guild halls, workshops and families whose houses are inspected every year by guild surveyors.

neighborhoods.name: The Quays
neighborhoods.summary: Grandport's working harbour: the dock office, bonded warehouses, cranes and the hiring line, where Ruestrian grain, Fresnian relics and Pictish furs are measured, taxed and insured.

neighborhoods.name: Shipwright Yards
neighborhoods.summary: Slipways where war carracks and merchant hulls rise in oak, with the long ropewalks and sail lofts behind them. Sawdust, tar and the shouts of the yard bells.

neighborhoods.name: The Lower Stairs
neighborhoods.summary: Steep alleys and stairs below the warehouses, home to rope girls, pressed sailors, guild militia widows and debtors. Hunger outlasted the siege here, and the Republic's critics say so.

neighborhoods.name: Ashrow
neighborhoods.summary: A district rebuilt in fresh oak after the last great fire, on merchant loans that are still being paid. The fire-watch tower and its bell stand at the top of the street.

neighborhoods.name: Admiralty Point
neighborhoods.summary: The navy's fortress at the harbour mouth, Admiral Horatio Horne's headquarters, and the signal tower whose flags and shuttered lanterns talk to the whole island chain.

neighborhoods.name: Old Gran Porte
neighborhoods.summary: The first harbour King Aelfred secured, with the oldest quays and the shuttered royal palace. The street where King Alrdric fell is here, and old loyalties are spoken of quietly.

neighborhoods.name: Chart House Hill
neighborhoods.summary: Where the Republic keeps its useful people: navigators, astronomers, engineers, printers and the public school, under the patronage of men like Magister Aldous Thorne.

neighborhoods.name: Strangers' Wharf
neighborhoods.summary: The wharf for foreign ships and foreign people: Ruestrian grain factors, Fresnian relic dealers, Pictish fur traders, and a small chapel of Sol Eternel kept by travelling missionaries.

neighborhoods.name: The Marsh Fields
neighborhoods.summary: Drained estuary land at the city's edge, behind dykes: barley and oat fields, cattle pasture, dairies and the market road into town.

places.name: Grandeholm Tower
places.summary: The great tower Edgar Grandeholm built and rarely leaves, ruling from its upper chambers while agents and informants climb the stairs with ledgers. Visitors get as far as the gate.

places.name: The Raft Gardens
places.summary: Walled pleasure gardens laid on the stone rafts, opened to the public on Republic Day and to anyone with a merchant's token the rest of the year.

places.name: The Gilded Ledger
places.summary: A dining house for merchant princes and their factors: beef from the Marsh Fields, Ruestrian wine and private rooms where contracts are signed over dessert.

places.name: Temple of Thalassar on the Rafts
places.summary: A rich shrine to the sea Titan, paid for by ship-owning houses who come to ask for calm water before their convoys sail.

places.name: The Silk Arcade
places.summary: A covered arcade of tailors, perfumers, ring makers and gold-thread embroiderers who dress the Merchant Circle in silks and scented oils.

places.name: The Weighing Room
places.summary: A quiet coffee and chocolate room where factors wait for an audience, pretending not to read each other's papers.

places.name: The Hall of the Two Houses
places.summary: Seat of the Republic: the Merchant Circle sits above, the commons' house below. Public galleries fill when tariffs or the royalist question come up.

places.name: Temple of Nomion
places.summary: The great temple of the Titan of law and contract, where disputes are arbitrated, oaths sworn and the largest contracts witnessed on the altar steps.

places.name: The Insurers' Exchange
places.summary: A loud stone hall where cargoes, hulls and convoy escorts are priced and insured, with the latest signal-tower news chalked on boards by the door.

places.name: The Inkwell
places.summary: Clerks' tavern under the counting houses, with ale, pies and arguments about interest rates until the watch calls the hour.

places.name: The Honest Scales
places.summary: A narrow coffee house where brokers trade rumours at standing desks and a coin is touched to the little brass scale at the door for Chryseon's luck.

places.name: Notaries' Row
places.summary: A lane of scriveners, seal cutters, paper sellers and ledger binders, the cheapest place in the city to get a letter written.

places.name: Hall of the Pile-Drivers and Masons
places.summary: The guild that drives oak piles to bedrock and inspects every joint in the city. Its surveyors' settling records go back generations.

places.name: Carpenters' Gable Hall
places.summary: The tallest gable on the street, built by the timber-framers to prove they could. Apprentices gather in its yard at dawn.

places.name: Gable Street Market
places.summary: Stalls under the overhangs selling bread, cheese, tools, cloth and second-hand guild coats.

places.name: The Crooked Joint
places.summary: A craftsmen's alehouse named as a joke: the only building in the quarter the guild surveyors have ever failed. A hurdy-gurdy player most nights.

places.name: Oak and Adze Workshop
places.summary: A joinery that takes small commissions: chests, cradles, ship models. Watchers are tolerated if they hold a plank now and then.

places.name: Widow Aldwen's Bakehouse
places.summary: Oat bread, barley rolls and honey cakes from a brick oven the guild insisted on before it would let her keep a fire.

places.name: The Dock Office
places.summary: Where every cargo is measured, taxed and recorded before it may leave the quay. The queue starts before sunrise.

places.name: The Grand Quay
places.summary: The long stone quay on oak piles where carracks unload, cranes creak and the hiring line forms each morning.

places.name: The Bonded Warehouses
places.summary: Rows of guarded warehouses where goods wait for their duties to be paid. Smells of pepper, pitch and Pictish furs.

places.name: The Fish Steps
places.summary: Morning fish market on the stone steps down to the water: herring, mackerel, eel and whatever the estuary boats bring.

places.name: The Drowned Lantern
places.summary: Sailors' tavern by the hiring line. Cheap ale, loud news from every port, and press-gang rumours that send men out the back door.

places.name: Mother Hild's Cookshop
places.summary: Bowls of fish stew and barley bread eaten standing at the counter between shifts.

places.name: The Great Slipways
places.summary: Slipways where the navy's high-castled carracks and the merchant hulls are framed in oak. Launch days draw crowds.

places.name: The Long Ropewalk
places.summary: A covered walk a quarter-mile long where rope girls spin hemp into cable, singing to keep the pace.

places.name: Canvas Loft
places.summary: Sailmakers cutting and stitching canvas on a floor so wide it is chalked like a map.

places.name: The Tar Pot
places.summary: Shipwrights' alehouse where the yard bell ends every argument. Fried eel and pickled onions.

places.name: Pell's Chandlery
places.summary: Everything for a ship: lanterns, pitch, compasses, salt pork and belaying pins (sold, the owner says, for sailing only).

places.name: Launch Green
places.summary: A patch of grass above the slipways where yard families picnic and children race toy hulls in the drainage pond.

places.name: The Hundred Steps
places.summary: The long stair from the warehouses down into the Lower Stairs, slick after rain, where people sit to talk because there is nowhere else to sit.

places.name: The Relief Hall
places.summary: Where Republican grain was handed out during the siege. It still gives bread on Relief Day, and people still argue about who it was for.

places.name: The Widows' Kitchen
places.summary: A soup kitchen and cheap eating house run by militia widows. Pay what you can; the pottage is the same either way.

places.name: The Blue Cloth
places.summary: A cellar tavern whose regulars still drink to the old Crown under their breath. Nobody admits what the faded blue cloth behind the bar once showed.

places.name: Shrine of Thalassar at the Stairs
places.summary: A niche shrine with a battered carved wave where sailors' families leave shells and candle stubs.

places.name: The Rag Market
places.summary: Second-hand clothes, mended boots, old sailcloth and pawned trinkets sold off blankets on the steps.

places.name: Ashrow Fire-Watch Tower
places.summary: The merchant-funded fire-watch tower with its great bell. Watchers sweep the rooftops all night for the first smoke.

places.name: New Oak Square
places.summary: The rebuilt square, its houses still pale fresh oak, with a well, benches and a loan broker's booth.

places.name: The Phoenix
places.summary: An alehouse whose first owner rebuilt it three times. Cheerful, crowded, and nervous about candles.

places.name: Ember Lane Pie Shop
places.summary: Beef and barley pies, eel pies and apple pasties sold hot through a window.

places.name: The Rain Barrel Baths
places.summary: A small bathhouse fed from the fire-watch cisterns, with a steam room and a wrestling floor.

places.name: The Admiralty Fortress
places.summary: The navy's harbour fortress, its walls patched with thicker stone round the gun ports. Admiral Horne keeps his quarters here.

places.name: The Signal Tower
places.summary: A granite base with a tall oak spire. Coloured flags by day and shuttered lanterns by night carry messages across the island chain in minutes.

places.name: Point Archery Butts
places.summary: Longbow butts below the fortress walls where the militia companies practise and anyone may pay for a dozen arrows.

places.name: The Powder and Plum
places.summary: Officers' tavern with a view of the harbour mouth. Plum brandy, roast fowl, and captains comparing commissions they bought.

places.name: The Mole Walk
places.summary: A path along the harbour mole to the outer light, windy, salty and popular with couples.

places.name: Aelfred's Quay
places.summary: The oldest quay, where King Aelfred first made the harbour a charge of the Crown. Now used by fishing boats and wherries.

places.name: The Shuttered Palace
places.summary: The old palace of House van Alnhalm, its banner lowered and windows boarded since the Revolution. The Republic has not decided what to do with it.

places.name: King's Fall Street
places.summary: The street where King Alrdric died trying to calm a hungry crowd. Republicans walk past; royalists leave a bread crust on the step.

places.name: The Old Horse
places.summary: An old coaching inn whose sign was repainted after the Revolution; the horse's crown still shows through in the rain.

places.name: Gran Porte Fish and Herb Market
places.summary: A small morning market under the old harbour wall: fish, herbs, eggs and island butter.

places.name: The Wherry Stairs
places.summary: A tea and coffee stall at the wherry landing, with benches facing the old harbour.

places.name: The Chart House
places.summary: Where Eadric Wyrmscraft's charts of Neokosmos are drawn, copied and sold, with the reconstructed Atlantean sextant shown on feast days.

places.name: The Hill Observatory
places.summary: A dome of oak and copper where Republic-funded astronomers time the stars for longitude tables. Open to visitors on clear nights for a coin.

places.name: The Republic Press
places.summary: The printing house that turns out the Ledger of Liberty, shipping lists and a weekly broadsheet the royalists call the Merchant's Gospel.

places.name: The Compass Rose
places.summary: Students' and navigators' tavern where bets are settled with dividers and every table has a chart scratched into it.

places.name: Booksellers' Steps
places.summary: Stalls of almanacs, tide tables, histories (both kinds), and sea romances.

places.name: The Thorne Library
places.summary: A subscription library endowed by Magister Aldous Thorne, open free to public school pupils.

places.name: The Strangers' Quay
places.summary: Where foreign ships must berth: Ruestrian grain galleys, Fresnian traders from the gulf and Pictish fur boats from the north.

places.name: Chapel of Sol Eternel
places.summary: A plain chapel kept by travelling missionaries like Aelric Stillhand, where Ruestrian sailors hear rites and curious locals listen at the door.

places.name: The Fur and Relic Market
places.summary: Pictish furs and carved bone beside Fresnian dealers swearing their Atlantean shards are genuine. Most are not.

places.name: Le Pain Solaire
places.summary: A Ruestrian cookhouse serving bread, lentils and wine the way the grain sailors like it.

places.name: De Gulden Kraan
places.summary: A Fresnian alehouse with red-brick walls brought as ballast, stepped gables painted on the sign and dark gulf beer.

places.name: The Silver Wake
places.summary: A late hall of music and dancers from every port, where exiles reinvent themselves nightly.

places.name: The Dyke Walk
places.summary: A path along the sea dyke with fields on one side and marsh birds on the other.

places.name: The Cattle Ground
places.summary: Weekly cattle and grain market where island farmers sell beef, barley and oats into the city.

places.name: Marsh Dairy House
places.summary: Buttermilk, fresh cheese and oatcakes served on a farmhouse bench by the dairy door.

places.name: The Barley Mow
places.summary: A farmers' alehouse at the city gate with its own brewhouse and the best barley ale on the island.

places.name: Dyke Mill
places.summary: The windmill that pumps the fields dry and grinds the barley, its sails visible from the signal tower.

colleges.name: Guild School of Piling and Masonry

employers.name: House Grandeholm
employers.summary: Edgar Grandeholm's trading, credit and insurance empire, with agents everywhere.

employers.name: House Thorne
employers.summary: Magister Aldous Thorne's naval trading house and patronage of the sciences.

employers.name: The Republic Admiralty
employers.summary: Admiral Horatio Horne's navy: carracks, galleys, fortresses and watchtowers.

employers.name: The Dock Office
employers.summary: Measures, taxes and records every cargo through the port.

employers.name: The Two Houses
employers.summary: The Republic's government: Merchant Circle, commons' house and their clerks.

employers.name: Guild of Pile-Drivers and Masons
employers.summary: Builds and inspects every foundation in Grandport.

employers.name: Carpenters' Guild
employers.summary: Timber-framers and joiners who raise the gables and rebuild after fires.

employers.name: The Great Yards
employers.summary: Slipways building navy carracks and merchant hulls.

employers.name: The Fire-Watch
employers.summary: Merchant-funded watchers, bells and bucket crews across the timber districts.

employers.name: Grandport Militia
employers.summary: District companies of longbowmen and pikemen, outfitted by merchant lords.

employers.name: The Chart House
employers.summary: Draws, corrects and sells charts under Republic patronage.

employers.name: The Republic Press
employers.summary: Prints histories, shipping lists and the weekly broadsheet.

employers.name: The Insurers' Exchange
employers.summary: Underwriters pricing hulls, cargoes and convoy escorts.

employers.name: Harbour taverns and cookshops
employers.summary: The alehouses, inns and cookshops along the waterfront.

employers.name: The Marsh Farms
employers.summary: Barley, oat and cattle farms behind the dykes.

career_hubs.name: The harbour
career_hubs.summary: Quays, warehouses, the dock office, taverns and foreign traders.

career_hubs.name: The Ledger Quarter and the Rafts
career_hubs.summary: Counting houses, insurers, the Two Houses and the merchant palaces.

career_hubs.name: The yards and the gables
career_hubs.summary: Slipways, ropewalks, guild workshops and the fire-watch.

career_hubs.name: Admiralty Point and the Hill
career_hubs.summary: The navy, the militia, the chart house, the press and the schools.

transit.name: Streets, stairs and alleys
transit.summary: Most people walk the narrow gabled streets and the stairs that climb from the quays.

transit.name: Harbour wherries
transit.summary: Rowing boats for hire between the quays, the yards, Admiralty Point and Gran Porte.

transit.name: Hired carriages
transit.summary: Few streets are wide enough; merchant houses keep carriages for the raft-palace avenues.

transit.name: The market road
transit.summary: The dyke road from the Marsh Fields into the city, busy with carts on market mornings.

climate.summary: Warm island sea weather: mild wet winters with gales, gentle summers, wind off the water most days. High rainfall keeps the fields green.

months.note: First fair days; the Two Houses sit.

annual_events.name: The Longbow Fair
annual_events.summary: District militia companies compete at the butts; archery is as much sport as duty here.

annual_events.name: The Settling Survey
annual_events.summary: Guild surveyors measure every building's yearly settling and chalk the marks on house corners.

annual_events.name: The Grain Fleet
annual_events.summary: Ruestrian grain galleys crowd the Strangers' Quay and bread prices finally fall.

annual_events.name: The Fur Boats
annual_events.summary: Pictish boats arrive with furs and deep-wood goods; the Fur and Relic Market doubles in size.

annual_events.name: Spring Launch
annual_events.summary: New carracks slide down the slipways before the season, with crowds on Launch Green.

annual_events.name: The Autumn Cattle Fair
annual_events.summary: The big autumn cattle and barley fair before winter feed runs short.

annual_events.name: Laying Up
annual_events.summary: Ships come home for the winter gales and sailors spend a season's pay in a week.

annual_events.name: The Spring Sitting
annual_events.summary: The Two Houses open their year; tariffs are argued and the galleries fill.

careers.name: Dockhand
careers.summary: Hauling cargo on the Grand Quay for a day wage, hired at the line each morning.

careers.name: Tide-waiter
careers.summary: A Dock Office officer who boards ships to measure and tax their cargo.

careers.name: Counting-house clerk
careers.summary: Copying ledgers, contracts and cargo lists in a stone-floored counting house.

careers.name: Merchant's factor
careers.summary: Buying, selling and negotiating for a great house in port and abroad.

careers.name: Underwriter
careers.summary: Pricing the risk on hulls and cargoes at the Insurers' Exchange.

careers.name: Courier
careers.summary: Running sealed letters between counting houses, palaces and the Two Houses.

careers.name: Arbiter of Nomion
careers.summary: Hearing disputes and witnessing contracts at the Temple of Nomion.

careers.name: Pile-driver
careers.summary: Driving oak piles through estuary silt to bedrock for new foundations.

careers.name: Guild mason
careers.summary: Cutting and laying ashlar for counting houses and merchant palaces.

careers.name: Guild surveyor
careers.summary: Inspecting joints and recording each house's yearly settling.

careers.name: Timber-framer
careers.summary: Raising oak frames and steep gables, and rebuilding after fires.

careers.name: Joiner
careers.summary: Making chests, panelling and furniture in a guild workshop.

careers.name: Shipwright
careers.summary: Framing and planking carracks and merchant hulls on the slipways.

careers.name: Caulker
careers.summary: Packing seams with oakum and hot pitch so the hulls stay dry.

careers.name: Sailmaker
careers.summary: Cutting and stitching canvas in the sail loft.

careers.name: Ropewalk spinner
careers.summary: Walking backwards down the ropewalk spinning hemp into cable.

careers.name: Sailor
careers.summary: Crewing a merchant or navy ship between the islands and foreign ports.

careers.name: Ship's man-at-arms
careers.summary: A professional boarding fighter with shield, seax and gambeson.

careers.name: Naval officer
careers.summary: A lieutenant or captain whose commission was most likely bought.

careers.name: Signal-keeper
careers.summary: Reading and sending flag and lantern signals across the island chain.

careers.name: Militia longbowman
careers.summary: A district militia archer who drills on rest days and works a trade otherwise.

careers.name: Fire-watcher
careers.summary: Watching the rooftops from a tower all night and ringing the bell at smoke.

careers.name: House guard
careers.summary: Guarding a merchant prince's palace, gates and secrets.

careers.name: House servant
careers.summary: Cooking, cleaning or waiting in a raft palace.

careers.name: Navigator
careers.summary: Fixing positions with sextant and tables, trained in the new Republic methods.

careers.name: Chart copyist
careers.summary: Copying and correcting charts at the Chart House.

careers.name: Printer
careers.summary: Setting type and pulling sheets at the Republic Press.

careers.name: Tavern keeper
careers.summary: Running an alehouse: barrels, regulars, debts and the watch.

careers.name: Tavern server
careers.summary: Carrying ale and gossip between tables, binding the regulars together.

careers.name: Cookshop cook
careers.summary: Stews, pies and bread for dockers and clerks.

careers.name: Tavern musician
careers.summary: Playing hurdy-gurdy, fiddle or pipes for coins and supper.

careers.name: Dancer
careers.summary: Dancing in the halls of Strangers' Wharf for coin and patrons.

careers.name: Fishmonger
careers.summary: Selling the night's catch on the Fish Steps.

careers.name: Baker
careers.summary: Baking oat and barley bread before dawn under guild fire rules.

careers.name: Farmhand
careers.summary: Working barley fields and dykes in the Marsh Fields.

careers.name: Dairy worker
careers.summary: Milking, churning and cheese-making at a marsh dairy.

careers.name: Drover
careers.summary: Bringing cattle down the market road to the Cattle Ground.

careers.name: Public school teacher
careers.summary: Teaching letters, sums and civics at the Republic's public school.

local_color.name: Beef and barley pie
local_color.summary: Island beef and barley in a thick crust, the everyday hot meal from the Marsh Fields to the quays.

local_color.name: Quay stew
local_color.summary: Whatever the boats brought, stewed with onions and eaten with barley bread.

local_color.name: Siege loaf
local_color.summary: A hard, dark ration loaf baked on Relief Day; old people eat it in silence.

local_color.name: Oatcakes and buttermilk
local_color.summary: The farm breakfast from the Marsh Fields.

local_color.name: Barley ale
local_color.summary: Brewed from island barley, brown and plain; every district argues whose is best.

local_color.name: Ruestrian red
local_color.summary: Imported wine, cheap on the wharf and dear on the Rafts.

local_color.name: Plum brandy
local_color.summary: The naval officers' drink, carried in flasks on watch.

local_color.name: "By Chryseon's scale"
local_color.summary: An oath sworn on deals and bets; Chryseon's name is spoken whenever coin is weighed.

local_color.name: "Ships that arrive sooner arrive richer"
local_color.summary: Eadric Wyrmscraft's line, now said about anything done promptly.

local_color.name: "The Crown brought soldiers; the Republic brought bread"
local_color.summary: Republican slogan from the siege; in the Lower Stairs it is usually said with a twist.

local_color.name: "Budget for the unseen"
local_color.summary: The builders' rule, after the oak piles under every house, used for any careful planning.

local_color.name: "What sank may yet rise"
local_color.summary: A royalist whisper, from Captain Sterling's history of the Crown beneath the waves.

local_color.name: Settling marks
local_color.summary: Every house corner carries chalk and chisel marks from the yearly settling survey; people read them like ages.

local_color.name: White and yellow
local_color.summary: The Republic's colours. A crowned horse on blue cloth is the old royal sign and is not shown openly.

local_color.name: Reading the flags
local_color.summary: Harbour children and idle clerks try to read the signal tower's flags before the news reaches the Exchange.

local_color.name: Fire rules
local_color.summary: Guild rules on chimneys, ovens and candles; neighbours report each other to the fire-watch without shame.

local_color.name: District longbow companies
local_color.summary: Militia archers wear their district's ribbon and the Longbow Fair settles a year of boasting.

prices.item: A dozen arrows at the butts

holidays.name: Republic Day
holidays.summary: The founding of the Republic, with white and yellow banners, speeches at the Two Houses and the Raft Gardens opened to all.

holidays.name: Relief Day
holidays.summary: The day Republican grain reached the besieged city; bread is handed out at the Relief Hall.

holidays.name: Fall Day
holidays.summary: New year of the A.F. reckoning, counted from the Fall of Atlantis; lanterns are set on the water for drowned cities.

holidays.name: Thalassar's Blessing
holidays.summary: The shipping season opens: priests of Thalassar bless the convoys and the whole harbour turns out.

holidays.name: Nomion's Day
holidays.summary: Leases, apprenticeships and yearly contracts renew; queues at the Temple of Nomion all day.

holidays.name: Chryseon's Night
holidays.summary: A coin is weighed and given away for luck in the coming year; counting houses close early.

holidays.name: Harbour Day
holidays.summary: Old Gran Porte's founding: boat races, fish suppers on Aelfred's Quay. Royalists drink to Aelfred, Republicans to the harbour.

holidays.name: Ash Day
holidays.summary: Remembering the last great fire; every fire-watch bell rings at noon and hearths are inspected.

holidays.name: Sol's Midsummer
holidays.summary: The faithful of Sol Eternel keep a dawn rite at the Strangers' Wharf chapel.

holidays.name: The Lowered Banner
holidays.summary: The anniversary of King Alrdric's death, kept only by royalists with bread crusts and quiet toasts.

notables.name: Edgar Grandeholm
notables.about: Founder of the Merchant Circle and its richest man: large, silk-clad, rings on nearly every finger. He rules contracts, insurance and harbour policy from the upper chambers of his tower and believes only in leverage.

notables.name: Aldous Thorne
notables.about: Author of The Ledger of Liberty and the Republic's idealist: austere dark wools, silver beard, sharp grey eyes. Led the militia in the siege and now patrons navigators and scholars.

notables.name: Horatio Horne
notables.about: The Merchant Circle founder who brought the ships: broad, copper-red hair and beard, gold-trimmed dark coats. Royalists call him a turncoat; he talks of hulls, powder and tides.

notables.name: Eadric Wyrmscraft
notables.about: A shipwright's son who rebuilt an Atlantean sextant and bounded the longitude problem; sharp, arrogant and usually right. Finishing his great book of the geography of Neokosmos.

notables.name: Aelric Stillhand
notables.role: merchant and missionary of Sol Eternel
notables.about: Alnhaman trader turned missionary, captain of the Sunnlad: thinning hair, broad bearded face, light blue eyes that listen. Keeps careful accounts of every faith he meets.

notables.name: Ceolmund
notables.about: A calm, honest trader known in many ports: stocky, salt-and-pepper beard, warm hazel eyes, dark overcoat and a ledger always to hand. Settles crew quarrels with a few measured words.

notables.name: Ceolwynn
notables.about: Ceolmund's quiet daughter, petite with soft brown eyes and her mother's pendant. Says little; her hurdy-gurdy says the rest, and sailors swear it steadies a whole room.

notables.name: Freydis
notables.about: Tall and athletic, black-dyed bob, icy blue eyes; an orphan raised by the merchant guild. Quick, funny and somehow a slightly different person each time you meet her.

notables.name: Ophir
notables.about: A former noblewoman turned dancer: tall, sun-tanned, long black hair, light blue eyes, white silk trimmed in gold. Every smile is calculated; she means to be powerful again.
